answer: Use a hardware meter ledger. Each identity earns only while a hardware-rooted meter signs continuous resource use; keys sharing a meter merge into one identity, and a jetty sensor can prove the meter’s site. An attacker must provision a distinct meter, power, and connectivity per clone—a karst site needs its own link—so cloning pays recurring infrastructure. Honest agents amortize one meter; a timber-frame rack does not help without a unique signed meter.
